headline_marked: Samsung to [[more than double]] HBM4 DRAM output next year, boosting glass carrier demand
headline: Samsung to more than double HBM4 DRAM output next year, boosting glass carrier demand
summary: The company plans to increase outsourced glass carrier cleaning volume by 2.5 times, with HBM4 family chips projected to make up 80% of shipments.
details: Samsung Electronics is set to more than double its output of HBM4 and HBM4E high-bandwidth memory chips in the coming year. This significant production increase is expected to drive a 2.5-fold rise in demand for glass carriers, a critical component in HBM manufacturing.

Glass carriers are essential for supporting HBM DRAM wafers during the thinning process, preventing bending or cracking. As HBM technology advances with higher layer stacking, the precision required for wafer thinning and warpage control becomes increasingly crucial.

The company plans to boost outsourced cleaning volume for glass carriers from 20,000 sheets per month this year to 50,000 sheets per month next year. This follows a doubling of demand from 10,000 sheets per month in 2023.

Samsung's HBM4 and HBM4E products, featuring 12-layer stacks and higher, are central to this expansion. The company began mass-producing HBM4 in February and provided HBM4E samples to customers like Nvidia in May.

Industry analysts anticipate Samsung's overall HBM production scale to grow by nearly 40% to approximately 250,000 wafers per month next year. The HBM4 family, including the high-value HBM4E, is projected to constitute about 80% of shipments, up from around 40% this year.
